name: PAUL BUNNEL TEST (MONOSPOT TEST FOR INFECTIOUS MONONUCLEOSIS)
interpretation:
Monospot test is a rapid test for the detection of heterophile antibody associated with Infectious mononucleosis.
Monospot test is a rapid agglutination test for use with human serum or EDTA plasma in the detection of the
heterophile antibody associated with infectious mononucleosis (IM).
Disclaimer:
A careful consideration to combination of epidemiological factors, stage of infection, clinical history, examination,
other relevant investigation findings and treatment history should be done when interpreting test results.
Test Limitations:
A low or suspected positive result should be re-assessed. Diagnosis should not be made solely on the findings of one clinical assay. When making an interpretation of the test it is strongly advised to take all clinical data into
consideration. Due to possible prozone effect, the strength of agglutination in the screening test is not indicative of
the IM heterophile antibody titre.IM heterophile antibody has been associated with several diseases other than IM. These include leukaemia, Burkitt’s Lymphoma, pancreatic carcinoma, viral hepatitis, CMV infections and others.
Clinical Reference:
Kim M, Wadke M. Comparative evaluation of two test methods (enzyme immunoassay and latex fixation) for the
detection of heterophil antibodies in infectious mononucleosis. J Clin Microbiol. 1990 Nov;28(11):2511–2513.
Axelrod P, Finestone AJ. Infectious mononucleosis in older adults. Am Fam Physician. 1990 Dec;42(6):1599–1606.
